info.title: kling/kling-3.0-turbo
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "kling/kling-3.0-turbo", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for a Kling 3.0 Turbo text-to-video generation. `prompt` is the one field Kling requires. The model is named by the route on both surfaces -- the v1 path ends in the model spelling and the Comfy Router path is /v2/models/kling/kling-3.0-turbo -- so the body carries no model field at all and the same `required` list serves both.

example.prompt: A neon-lit alley in the rain, slow dolly forward.

prompt.description: Prompt that may include both positive and negative descriptions. Recommended length under 2500 characters. Multi-shot videos use the format "shot n, m, words; shot n, m, words;".

settings.description: Output configuration such as resolution, aspect ratio and duration.

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio (width:height) of the generated frames. One of "16:9", "9:16" or "1:1". Default "16:9".

duration.description: Video length in seconds. Supported values 3 through 15. Default 5.

resolution.description: Clarity of the generated video. One of "720p" or "1080p". Default "720p".

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for Kling 3.0 Turbo: the terminal `GET /tasks?task_ids={id}` document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is submit-and-poll — `routerresult/classification.go` records `{provider: kling, endpoint: /text-to-video/kling-3.0-turbo}` as `ReturnModeSubmitPoll` — and Router polls on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is the finished task rather than the `data.id` handle the underlying submit answers with.
This is NOT the document the eleven Kling v1 video ids answer (`KlingVideoRouterOutput`), and the three differences are the reason it is its own component. `data` is a LIST — one element per task id the query named — rather than a single object, so the generated video's download URL is at `data[].outputs[].url`, under the element for the polled task. Router always polls ONE task (the poll route is built from the single id the submit returned, so the request is always `?task_ids=<one id>`), so that list carries one element in practice; a caller polling this route directly with several ids gets one element each and must match on `data[].id`. Second, the terminal status spells `succeeded`, where every v1 Kling route says `succeed`. Third, the outputs live under `outputs[]` rather than `task_result`.
Read the ELEMENT field, not the `outputs` container: `KlingV2Output` is `{type, id, url, watermark_url, duration, ...}`, so a one-element list carrying an id and a type and no URL is a non-empty array holding nothing playable. `data[].outputs[].watermark_url` is the same asset under Kling's hotlink-protection form and counts as a result. `mp3_url` and `wav_url` deliberately do NOT: the operation Router serves here is text-to-video, so a success carrying only audio is a shape anomaly. `routerpollstate.classifyKlingV2` draws exactly those lines.
`url` is hotlink-protected and Kling clears it after 30 days, so download it rather than storing the link.

KlingV2Options.description: General configuration such as callback address and watermark options.

callback_url.description: Callback notification URL for task results. The server notifies when the task status changes.

external_task_id.description: Customized Task ID. Does not overwrite the system-generated task ID but can be used for queries. Must be unique within a single user account.

watermark_info.description: Whether to generate watermarked results simultaneously. Custom watermarks are not supported.

enabled.description: true means generate watermarked result, false means do not generate. Default false.

KlingV2Output.description: A generated output. The fields present depend on `type` (video, image, audio, voice or element).

duration.description: Duration of the generated video in seconds.

group_id.description: Grouping marker, present only for grouped images.

id.description: Output ID generated by the system.

mp3_duration.description: Duration of the generated MP3 audio in seconds.

mp3_url.description: MP3 URL of the generated audio (hotlink-protected).

owned_by.description: Source of the material. "kling" denotes the official library; numbers are creator IDs.

status.description: Status of the material. One of "succeeded" or "deleted".

type.description: Output content type. One of "video", "image", "audio", "voice" or "element".

url.description: URL of the generated result (hotlink-protected). Cleared after 30 days.

wav_duration.description: Duration of the generated WAV audio in seconds.

wav_url.description: WAV URL of the generated audio (hotlink-protected).

KlingV2QueryTaskResponse.description: Response returned when querying Kling 3.0 Turbo tasks by ID.

request_id.description: Request ID generated by the system.

KlingV2Task.description: A single Kling 3.0 Turbo task record.

amount.description: Consumption amount, accurate to two decimal places.

charge_type.description: Consumption account type. "cash" for balance, "unit" for a resource package.

package_type.description: Consumable resource bundle type (only present when charge_type is "unit"). One of "video", "image" or "audio".

create_time.description: Task creation time. Unix timestamp in milliseconds.

external_id.description: The custom task ID for this task, if any.

message.description: Task status information, displaying the failure reason when the task fails.

update_time.description: Task update time. Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
